raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

ZeRO stages 1 and 2 update optimizer parameter groups one at a time and call
`_lazy_init_hp_params_optimizer_state()` after each group. That method linked
whatever optimizer state existed at that moment and then unconditionally set
`_hp_optimizer_states_linked = True`. Groups that had not been stepped yet
therefore never linked their Adam moments after their own update, and
`safe_get_full_optimizer_state()` raised:

```
ValueError: exp_avg not found in optimizer state fragment
```

for every group after the first.

This change:

- makes `lazy_init_hp_params_optimizer_state()` report whether a group's
  optimizer state exists yet, and set the fragments for that group;
- passes the just-stepped group index from `_optimizer_step()` so only that
  group is inspected, and tracks linked groups individually. A group that still
  has no state is retried on its next update, so the work per group update is
  bounded by one group rather than a rescan of all of them;
- keeps `_hp_optimizer_states_linked` false until every group has been linked;
- adds a two-rank regression test with separate `weight` and `bias` parameter
  groups for ZeRO stages 1 and 2, asserting both moments after the first step;
- adds a unit test pinning that linking after a group update inspects only that
  group.

`BF16_Optimizer` shares the helper but is not affected: it calls `step()` once
for all parameter groups before linking, so every group already has its state.
That wrapper is unchanged.

Fixes #8911.

## Duplicate-work check

As of master `27360990020b0619b744e5fc5e6e4d6e9de3fb79` (2026-10-30):

- `gh issue view 8911 --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --comments`: no comments.
- `gh pr list --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --state open --search "8911 in:body"`:
  no matching PR.
- No open PR in the ZeRO 1/2 optimizer-state path addresses this defect.

## Tests

Environment: Apple M2 Pro (arm64), macOS 27.2, CPU accelerator with Gloo,
Python 3.12.9, torch 2.15.0, DeepSpeed 0.19.9 built from this branch.

```bash
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PWD/tests"
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 LOCAL_SIZE=2 PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1  # bypass /proc/cpuinfo discovery on macOS
DS_ACCELERATOR=cpu python -m pytest -p pytest_forked --forked \
  tests/unit/runtime/zero/test_zero_tensor_fragment.py::TestOptimizerStateLinksAllParamGroups \
  tests/unit/runtime/zero/test_zero_tensor_fragment.py::test_lazy_init_only_inspects_the_group_that_stepped \
  tests/unit/runtime/zero/test_zero_tensor_fragment.py::TestZeroBf16Fp32GradAccum
```

- With the fix: **9 passed** (the stage 1 and stage 2 regression cases, the new
  per-group unit test, and the existing stage 1 BF16 wrapper, stage 2
  CPU-offload, stage 2 non-contiguous, and stage 3 gradient tests).
- With only the production changes reverted: the two regression cases fail with
  `ValueError: exp_avg not found in optimizer state fragment`.
- The new per-group unit test fails against an implementation that rescans every
  group on each update, so it pins the bounded-work behavior.
- `tests/unit/v1/zero/test_zero2_gradient_safety.py` and
  `tests/unit/v1/zero/test_invalid_grad_norm.py`: 47 passed, 2 skipped, and one
  pre-existing failure from the macOS CPU op builder (`KeyError: 'flags'` in
  `op_builder/cpu/builder.py`), unrelated to this change.

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks passed.

## Compatibility matrix

| Cell | Validated |
| --- | --- |
| ZeRO stage 1, bf16, Adam, 2 ranks | Yes (new regression) |
| ZeRO stage 2, bf16, Adam, 2 ranks | Yes (new regression) |
| ZeRO stage 1 BF16_Optimizer wrapper | Yes (existing `TestZeroBf16Fp32GradAccum[stage1]`) |
| ZeRO stage 2 CPU optimizer offload | Yes (existing sibling test) |
| ZeRO stage 2 non-contiguous gradients | Yes (existing sibling test) |
| ZeRO stage 3 | Unaffected; existing sibling test passed |
| fp16 | Not run (CPU test host has no fp16 support) |
| CUDA | Not run locally |
| MoE / EP | Not run |

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to investigate the issue, implement the change, and run
the tests. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and signed off the
commits.

When the wrapped optimizer legitimately has no per-parameter state, such as `torch.optim.SGD(momentum=0)`, `optimizer_state.get(...)` remains `None` or `{}` after every successful update, so this returns `False` forever. nodes.body:
Good catch — that is a real regression, and it is fixed in 8b1f41e.

The hook is no longer a rescan. `_optimizer_step()` now passes the group it just updated, `_lazy_init_hp_params_optimizer_state(group_no)` inspects only that group, and linked groups are tracked in a set, so an already-linked group returns immediately. A group whose state appears later is retried on its own next update.

For a stateless optimizer the helper still returns `False` every time, but the cost per group update is now one `optimizer.state.get()` and a no-op fragment set for that single group, instead of walking all N groups and rebuilding the mappings of the stateful ones. The global flag stays false in that case, which is harmless because it is only used as the fast path inside this method.

I did not mark a stateless group complete from state-dict truthiness, because a stateful optimizer can legitimately leave a group without state (for example a group whose params have no gradients yet), and that group still has to link once its state appears. The per-group retry handles both cases without the quadratic scan.

I also reverted the `BF16_Optimizer` change: that wrapper calls `step()` once for all groups before linking, so every group already has state there and it never had the ordering defect.

Added `test_lazy_init_only_inspects_the_group_that_stepped`, which fails against the previous scan-all implementation and passes now.

Read at `8b1f41ec`.

The fix looks right to me. Each group is linked after its own update, and a group is recorded as linked only once the optimizer has state for it.

On CPU (gloo), I ran a two-group check against a plain `torch.optim.AdamW` reference, with weight decay on the matrices and off for the rest, for ZeRO-1 and ZeRO-2. `safe_get_full_optimizer_state` matches `exp_avg` and `exp_avg_sq` for every parameter on this branch, at DP=1 and DP=2. On master the same check fails at DP=1 with `exp_avg not found in optimizer state fragment`. Your three new tests pass here too.

This overlaps with #8643, which fixes the same bug the same way: per-group linking, keyed on the `group_no` that `_optimizer_step` just stepped. It has been open since September, and the two conflict in `stage_1_and_2.py` and `test_zero_tensor_fragment.py`. The duplicate check in the description searched for `8911`, which #8643 predates. Its AdamW-reference test, adapted to a client AdamW, passes on this branch, and your regression cases pass on #8643. The one behavioural difference: this PR waits until a group actually has state before marking it linked, while #8643 marks it after its first step. Maintainers will probably want to pick one.

One related gap, from reading the code rather than running it: `load_hp_checkpoint_state` always resets `optim_fragment` to `{}`, and only an optimizer-state load relinks it. After a weights-only universal load into an engine that has already stepped, every group is still in `_hp_optimizer_states_linked_groups`, so the fragments are never relinked. `safe_get_full_optimizer_state` then raises. The `_hp_optimizer_states_linked_groups` set added here is the natural place to fix it.

From reading the code, not from a run. This per-group set is now the only thing that triggers relinking. A universal load with `load_optimizer_states=False` empties every fragment (`load_hp_checkpoint_state` resets `optim_fragment`), but leaves the groups recorded as linked. In `_load_universal_checkpoint`, clearing the set and the flag and then calling `_lazy_init_hp_params_optimizer_state()` with no group, your retry-all path, would relink at load time. Clearing alone would leave the getters failing until the next step.

Fixed in 7411b74. `_load_universal_checkpoint()` now resets `_hp_optimizer_states_linked`, clears `_hp_optimizer_states_linked_groups`, and then calls `_lazy_init_hp_params_optimizer_state()` with no group, so the retry-all path relinks whatever state is still in memory. Groups without state stay pending and link on their next update, which keeps `load_optimizer_states=False` behaving the same as before for engines that never stepped.

`TestUniversalLoadKeepsOptimizerStateLinked` steps once, clears every `optim_fragment` to simulate a weights-only universal load, calls `_load_universal_checkpoint(..., load_optimizer_states=False)`, and asserts the getters still return the pre-load moments. It fails on 8b1f41e with `ValueError: exp_avg not found in optimizer state fragment`, and passes now for ZeRO-1 and ZeRO-2 at DP=2 on CPU/gloo.

I scoped this to the universal load path you pointed at. `_link_all_hp_params()` also rebuilds fragments during a legacy load and during offload reload, so the same invalidation may belong there too. I have not changed those paths because I cannot exercise optimizer-state offload on this CPU-only host; say the word if you want that included here.

nodes.body:
Thanks, 7411b74 works. I checked it with a real round trip rather than the stubbed load: two param groups, ZeRO-1 and ZeRO-2, one step, `save_checkpoint`, `ds_to_universal`, then a universal `load_checkpoint(..., load_optimizer_states=False)` into the same engine. On 7411b74 the getters return the pre-load moments; on 8b1f41e they raise `exp_avg not found in optimizer state fragment`.

On your question: yes, I think the other two paths belong here, since this set is now what decides relinking. Both reproduce on CPU, and both fail the same way on master with a single group, so they're older than this PR:

- Legacy `load_checkpoint` with optimizer states into an engine that has already stepped: `_link_all_hp_params()` builds new mappings with `optim_fragment = None`, so the getters raise `TypeError` until something relinks.
- `offload_states(include=[hp_params])` then `reload_states()`: same `TypeError`.
- `optim_states` offload/reload is quieter. `reload_optimizer_states` replaces each state tensor (`state[k] = v.to(device)`), so the fragments keep pointing at the old tensors, and after the next step the getters return stale moments without raising. On CPU the move keeps tensor identity, so I emulated it by replacing the state tensors with copies; I haven't run this on a GPU.

Relinking inside `_link_all_hp_params()` fixes the first two but not the third, because `reload_states` relinks the hp params before the optimizer states come back. What passed every case for me (legacy, both universal loads, hp/optim/both offload-reload; ZeRO-1 and 2; two groups) was a small helper called after the legacy link and once at the end of `reload_states`:

```python
def _relink_hp_optimizer_states(self):
    self._hp_optimizer_states_linked = False
    self._hp_optimizer_states_linked_groups.clear()
    self._lazy_init_hp_params_optimizer_state()
```

inline_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mark successfully stepped stateless groups complete**

When the wrapped optimizer legitimately has no per-parameter state, such as `torch.optim.SGD(momentum=0)`, `optimizer_state.get(...)` remains `None` or `{}` after every successful update, so this returns `False` forever. Both wrappers therefore keep `_hp_optimizer_states_linked` false; in ZeRO-1/2 the helper is invoked after every per-group update, turning every training step into an O(number-of-groups²) rescan and repeatedly rebuilding mappings for any stateful sibling groups. Track whether a group has already been stepped separately, or otherwise mark a stateless group complete, rather than using state-dictionary truthiness as the completion signal.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

inline_comments.body:
Good catch — that is a real regression, and it is fixed in 8b1f41e.

The hook is no longer a rescan. `_optimizer_step()` now passes the group it just updated, `_lazy_init_hp_params_optimizer_state(group_no)` inspects only that group, and linked groups are tracked in a set, so an already-linked group returns immediately. A group whose state appears later is retried on its own next update.

For a stateless optimizer the helper still returns `False` every time, but the cost per group update is now one `optimizer.state.get()` and a no-op fragment set for that single group, instead of walking all N groups and rebuilding the mappings of the stateful ones. The global flag stays false in that case, which is harmless because it is only used as the fast path inside this method.

I did not mark a stateless group complete from state-dict truthiness, because a stateful optimizer can legitimately leave a group without state (for example a group whose params have no gradients yet), and that group still has to link once its state appears. The per-group retry handles both cases without the quadratic scan.

I also reverted the `BF16_Optimizer` change: that wrapper calls `step()` once for all groups before linking, so every group already has state there and it never had the ordering defect.

Added `test_lazy_init_only_inspects_the_group_that_stepped`, which fails against the previous scan-all implementation and passes now.

Fixed in 7411b74. `_load_universal_checkpoint()` now resets `_hp_optimizer_states_linked`, clears `_hp_optimizer_states_linked_groups`, and then calls `_lazy_init_hp_params_optimizer_state()` with no group, so the retry-all path relinks whatever state is still in memory. I scoped this to the universal load path you pointed at. `_link_all_hp_params()` also rebuilds fragments during a legacy load and during offload reload, so the same invalidation may belong there too. I have not changed those paths because I cannot exercise optimizer-state offload on this CPU-only host; say the word if you want that included here.

Thanks, 7411b74 works. I checked it with a real round trip rather than the stubbed load: two param groups, ZeRO-1 and ZeRO-2, one step, `save_checkpoint`, `ds_to_universal`, then a universal `load_checkpoint(..., load_optimizer_states=False)` into the same engine. On 7411b74 the getters return the pre-load moments; on 8b1f41e they raise `exp_avg not found in optimizer state fragment`.

On your question: yes, I think the other two paths belong here, since this set is now what decides relinking. Both reproduce on CPU, and both fail the same way on master with a single group, so they're older than this PR:

- Legacy `load_checkpoint` with optimizer states into an engine that has already stepped: `_link_all_hp_params()` builds new mappings with `optim_fragment = None`, so the getters raise `TypeError` until something relinks.
- `offload_states(include=[hp_params])` then `reload_states()`: same `TypeError`.
- `optim_states` offload/reload is quieter. `reload_optimizer_states` replaces each state tensor (`state[k] = v.to(device)`), so the fragments keep pointing at the old tensors, and after the next step the getters return stale moments without raising. On CPU the move keeps tensor identity, so I emulated it by replacing the state tensors with copies; I haven't run this on a GPU.

Relinking inside `_link_all_hp_params()` fixes the first two but not the third, because `reload_states` relinks the hp params before the optimizer states come back. Read at `8b1f41ec`.

The fix looks right to me. Each group is linked after its own update, and a group is recorded as linked only once the optimizer has state for it.

On CPU (gloo), I ran a two-group check against a plain `torch.optim.AdamW` reference, with weight decay on the matrices and off for the rest, for ZeRO-1 and ZeRO-2. `safe_get_full_optimizer_state` matches `exp_avg` and `exp_avg_sq` for every parameter on this branch, at DP=1 and DP=2. On master the same check fails at DP=1 with `exp_avg not found in optimizer state fragment`. Your three new tests pass here too.

This overlaps with #8643, which fixes the same bug the same way: per-group linking, keyed on the `group_no` that `_optimizer_step` just stepped. It has been open since September, and the two conflict in `stage_1_and_2.py` and `test_zero_tensor_fragment.py`. The duplicate check in the description searched for `8911`, which #8643 predates. Its AdamW-reference test, adapted to a client AdamW, passes on this branch, and your regression cases pass on #8643. The one behavioural difference: this PR waits until a group actually has state before marking it linked, while #8643 marks it after its first step. Maintainers will probably want to pick one.

One related gap, from reading the code rather than running it: `load_hp_checkpoint_state` always resets `optim_fragment` to `{}`, and only an optimizer-state load relinks it. After a weights-only universal load into an engine that has already stepped, every group is still in `_hp_optimizer_states_linked_groups`, so the fragments are never relinked. `safe_get_full_optimizer_state` then raises. The `_hp_optimizer_states_linked_groups` set added here is the natural place to fix it.
